title: Dharana
description: Develop the power of single-pointed concentration, the essential precursor to meditation and the key to mental clarity.

sutra.meaning: Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga

sections.practice: attempt to take up one new practice or change in lifestyle in accordance with yamas and niyamas
sections.gurudevInsight: The husk is gone, the sprout moves though it & comes up. They are (1) Yama (2) Niyama (3) Aasana (4) Pranayama (5) Pratyahara (6) Dhyana (7) Dharana (8) Samadhi. He goes into the details of each & what is the result that you can expect from each one of them. Yoga has 8 limbs, like a chair has got four legs, yoga has 8 limbs, or legs. So you just pull 80 one, everything else will come down. If you pull one leg of the chair whole chair comes. [PDF p.80]

sutra.sanskrit:
त॒तः॒ क्षी॒य॒ते प्रकाशा॑वर॒णम्
धा॒र॒णासु च योग्यता॑ मन॒सः
sutra.meaning: From that is dissipated, the mental darkness which veils the light, ... and from that, is attained the state of the mind for linking the attention to a higher concentration force or person.

sections.insight: Pranayama removes the veil covering the light of knowledge and heralds the dawn of wisdom. The mind becomes fit, thereafter, for Dharana or concentration.. the next limb of yoga.Once the mind is still and free of thought it can focus on a single point. This is when it can manifest what it wants.
sections.practice: Make a commitment and effort to intensify your practice. Meditate for 20 min
sections.gurudevInsight: THE 8 LIMBS OF YOGA : Human consciousness is like a seed: - The seed has the possibility of a tree, of the leaves, of the branches, of the roots, of the flowers, of the fruits, of multiplication. A seeds needs a proper ground, proper conditions, sunlight, water, proper soil for it to sprout & blossoms, isn’t it? Same is the case with the human consciousness, human mind. Either the seed can be dormant for years together, keeping its possibility within itself or start blossoming, start sprouting; the spouting of the seed of human consciousness is viveka, Discrimination, wisdom. Freedom comes with viveka or discrimination. [PDF p.80]

sutra.meaning: Fixing the consciousness on one point or region is Dharana.

sections.insight: The yogi must be so familiar with the realm of his mind and emotions, that he should begin to recognize where the thoughts, ideas, images and memories are arising. . Then he can practice the sixth stage of yoga, which is putting his attention to a single object or region.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is my mind quiet enough to permit me to focus on a single object for a significant duration of my meditation.
sections.practice: Practice focusing on a part of your body, say the heart with eyes closed.
sections.gurudevInsight: You are the light but you do not know because there is a thick curtain around you, an iron curtain around you & this thins down the iron curtain & makes it more transparent that you are able to see that you are light. Another benefit dharanasachayogyatamanasa your mind gets this ability to stay at any one point in the body, to stay at any one point in the body, to stay on any one thing, it is against the ability to intend. Till now there was no intention, you were just like a crowd moving, there was no you inside, you had no intention at all. You are able to have an intention, a direction. [PDF p.92]

sutra.meaning: Focused awareness on one object stabilizes the mind

sections.reflectionPrompt: Bring your attention to your breath
sections.practice: Observe breathing for as long as it takes to go into meditation.
sections.gurudevInsight: “Prachardanvidharanbhya va pranasya” In a special manner modulating the prana & the breath. By this also your mind becomes calm & one pointed, one focused, hmm! Another Sutra: “vishayvati va pravrutirutpanna manastithinibandhani” Suppose this doesn’t work, it does work but if you feel that still little incompletion is there, then through any one object of senses, the mind can be stilled, you are gazing, what is happening in gazing? You are looking at somebody, for a few moments, you gaze from all your heart, your mind that time is not running here & there. [PDF p.40]

sutra.meaning: Mastery extends from smallest to largest

sections.practice: Observe deeply everything you see today.
sections.gurudevInsight: Discipline of YOGA Patanjali yoga sutras begins. Atha yoganushashanam Now, we will look into the discipline of Yoga. Now I will enunciate the discipline of Yoga. Shashana mean rules that somebody else puts on you. Anushashana is the rule that you put, impose on yourself. [PDF p.7]

sutra.meaning: The seer the seen and the instrument of perception become one.When mind becomes clear it reflects reality like a crystal

sections.insight: When the mind is pure it reflects truth without distortion.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is my perception clear or colored?
sections.gurudevInsight: If you do this, you chita, your mind will be pleasant. In that gracious, graceful mind, one pointedness becomes very much easy, very simple, hmm! Practice one thing or devotion to one thing or one aspect. Ok, Even that becomes difficult, he says, there is another sutra. “Prachardanvidharanbhya va pranasya” Breaking the rhythms of the breath, the natural rhythms of the breath & holding the breath, sustaining the breath in different rhythms. If someone asks you, where did Patanjali talked about kriya, Patanjali has not mentioned about Sudarshan kriya directly. [PDF p.40]
